recipes.name: Chicken Apple Sausage with Cabbage
ingredients_raw: salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
1 pound small Yukon Gold potatoes, scrubbed but not peeled
2 tablespoons chopped fresh parsley, for garnish

steps.text: Combine butter and olive oil in a Dutch oven over medium heat. When butter melts, add sausage links; cook until browned on all sides, 6 to 8 minutes.
Stir in onion and season with salt and pepper; cook and stir until onion is slightly translucent and caramelized, about 5 minutes. Add garlic; cook and stir until fragrant, about 30 seconds.

Pour in apple cider, increase heat to medium-high, and stir in potatoes; bring to a simmer. Pour cabbage over sausage mixture and reduce heat to medium-low. Cover and simmer until potatoes are tender, 20 to 25 minutes. Transfer sausage links and potatoes to a plate.
Increase heat to high and simmer liquid until thick and reduced by half, about 5 minutes. Return sausage links and potatoes to the pot. Remove from the heat and season with salt and pepper.
Garnish servings with mustard and parsley.

raw_recipe.headline: Chicken Apple Sausage with Cabbage
raw_recipe.description: This chicken apple sausage recipe is a classic winter dish of sausage, cabbage, and potatoes. It's simple to make and a delight to eat any time of the year!

review.reviewBody: Only 2 reviews? Don't worry about that take my word for it. This is SO good! I've made it twice already and it is a hit! I changed a couple of things but basically stuck to the plan. I did not use the the Dijon or parsley, not needed. I did it the same except instead of cooking on the stove for 25 mins, I baked it in a covered enameled cast iron Dutch oven. I saute'd the sausages, then onions & I added a shallot with the garlic saute. Layered it with sausages & potatoes on bottom, then cabbage on top. Baked for about 45 mins covered at 375*. I thickened it before serving with whole grain organic baby rice cereal while on stove. No gluten!

Thank you Chef John for another stellar recipe...I followed the ingredients and directions to a “T”.....up to #3. After that I put the potatoes, pan cooked ingredients into my cast iron Dutch oven. Poured in the apple juice, added two carrots and put the cabbage on the top of everything..then sprinkled caraway seeds over everything. Put it in the oven at 350 for 45 minutes. (From someone else’s suggestion..cuz I have a problem with not using my cast iron Dutch oven when I can)...The texture and flavors together are amazing...Serve with your favorite tart wine (Chardonnay, or German style beer) AMAZING.

I read through all of the reviews before making this and a couple of adjustments or tips made this dish great. My husband and I eat mostly a vegetarian diet and I found some non GMO tofu Chicken Apple Sausages at the grocery store. I did cut up the potatoes into eighths and I used a spiced apple cider from Trader Joe's. I didn't remove the potatoes just let it simmer down and the consistency is perfect. Can't wait for my husband to come home and try it! (note if you are going with the veggie sausages then cook them in the oil and butter and put them aside until you are ready to serve, stir in and eat. The sausages cook so fast they are easy to overcook and you want them to be just right). ENJOY!
This is so yummy! I used spicy and sweet sausage 8 links total. I also added 3 Granny Smith apples peeled and chopped in big chunks. Excellent.

Turned out fantastic
Used red cabbage instead of green, added two cut granny smith apples along with the cabbage, and finished cooking with a splash of red wine vinegar

This is delicious! I used homemade bone broth and added chopped apples. I add beans to everything, so some creamy Brazilian pink beans went in the pot. I don’t cook with oil; and everything came out tender and creamy. So healthy and hits all my anti-inflammatory checkboxes.

This is a great recipe and I will make it again; I did make some changes. I used 3 cups of chicken broth (I didn't have apple juice), I added apples and I used a 16 oz bag of shredded cole slaw mix. The chicken broth gave it a great flavor, next time I will do 2 c broth and 1 c apple juice. I did #6, but nothing happened...it never thickened. That's OK it was still great. Thank you Chef John!

Used sweet Italian sausage, added two peeled and cored apples cut into large chunks (added layer of apples just before adding the cabbage). I used only apple cider and added a teaspoon or so of chicken bullion paste to help flavor during the 5 minute boil down. The mustard is a must (on the side to dip sausage into) as it adds great contrast. Sweet, hardy, tangy........YUM!

We loved it!!! Will definitely make again. So easy! Used regular smoked sausage, quality apple cider, and replaced a little cabbage with two large unpeeled Granny Smith apples. Great sweet-tart flavor! Stopped after simmering 25 minutes; remaining steps are unnecessary.

I added 2 chopped apples and didn't have apple sausage so used bratwurst. I added some white wine to the apple juice and was great. I probably would add more sausages as a lot of cabbage to meat. But then again, i estimated the "1.5 lbs" so may have used more. I also added a couple bay leaves. Delicious! I'm used to sauerkraut with sausage so this is a lightly sweet version of cabbage that is great!

I don't know yet - this is in the crock pot to put on first thing tomorrow. I am encouraged by some reviews, discouraged by others, but hopeful! I added about a tablespoon of apple cider vinegar, and half the apple juice. Also went ahead and added the mustard to the dish. I'll update after tomorrow....after I find a great loaf of rye to accompany it!

Easy and tasty! Next time I will try to remember to count the little potatoes as I add them to the pot. Then I will know exactly how many to hunt for when it is time to remove them to the covered dish while the cider reduces. I used a bagged coleslaw mix of shedded cabbage with carrots. Delicious!

This is one of our favorite easy meals. It can take a while to cook on the stovetop so I have made it both using the slow cooker (on IP) and the pressure cook using IP. I like to add some thinly sliced apples and caraway seeds and then serve with a crusty sourdough and the Dijon mustard.
Easy skillet dinner, made it exactly like the recipe stated. Both husband and I liked it well enough to put it into my "regular rotation" of recipes.
Great!! Added apples also, but I kinda added everything to the pot together and simmered and came out awesome!
I added a couple of chopped Granny Smith apples with the potatoes. We thought this was good and healthy comfort food.
Fabulous recipe, easy and delicious. Will definitely become a fall favorite for my family.
Made as written. We preferred it without the Dijon mustard.
Love it, this is the second time I’ve made this off of this recipe and it’s very tasty!

This was a really tasty recipe and my husband and I both very much enjoyed it. I was looking for something a little different and it looked so good. 
I personally find chicken sausage just slightly wanting and am not sure how to get around that for this recipe. I’ll make it again though. Very good!
